name: Field Doctor-Style Field Green Risotto (Low FODMAP)
ingredients:
360 g Broccoli
355 g Whole grain rice
320 g Edamame (SOY bean)
320 g Soy Milk [SOY beans, water]
200 g Spinach
1 medium Courgette
160 g Extra Virgin Olive Oil
80 g Peas
80 g Fennel
80 g Parmigiano (MILK) [MILK Salt, Microbial Enzymes]
80 g Chives
60 g Tapioca Starch
3 1/2 tbsp Pine Nuts
8 tbsp Mixed Herbs
4 tbsp Basil
3 1/2 tbsp Parsley Flat
1 tbsp Sea Salt
2 tbsp Lemon Zest
1/2 tsp Celery Salt (CELERY)
directions:
1. Prep veg: Cut broccoli, courgette and fennel small. Have spinach, peas, edamame, chives, basil and parsley ready.

2. Soften aromatics: Warm olive oil with chives and fennel until soft. Add broccoli, courgette, peas and edamame; cook a few minutes.

3. Risotto: Toast wholegrain rice in the pan 1–2 minutes. Add hot water (and a little soy milk for creaminess) gradually, stirring, until rice is creamy and just tender. Season with sea salt, celery salt and lemon zest.

4. Finish: Fold in spinach until wilted. Off heat, stir in hard cheese, herb mix, basil, parsley and a tapioca slurry only if you need more body. Top portions with toasted pine nuts.
 
Cool, portion into 8, refrigerate up to 3 days or freeze; reheat until piping hot.

Ingredients: Broccoli, Whole grain rice, Edamame (SOY bean), Soy Milk [SOY beans, water], Spinach, Spinach, Courgette, Extra Virgin Olive Oil...

Home recreation inspired by Field Doctor Field Green Risotto (Low FODMAP) (~394 g ready meal). Scaled to 8 portions. Not an official Field Doctor recipe. https://www.fielddoctor.co.uk/products/fod-field-green-risotto
notes:
REVERSE-ENGINEERED from Field Doctor published ingredients for personal home cooking only. Official meal is Monash Low FODMAP certified at single-serve size.

Scaling notes
Scaled for 8 portions from Field Doctor single serve (~394 g x 8 = 3152 g).
Unlabelled amounts inferred from UK descending-weight ingredient order (each item <= the one above and >= the one below; leftover mass shared on that basis, not equally).
Spoon measures use ingredient density (g per tsp) then round to kitchen fractions.
Amounts above 50 g are rounded to the nearest 5 g for cooking convenience.
Sweet peppers ~140 g each; carrots ~80 g; sweet potatoes ~130 g; courgettes ~175 g; aubergines ~250 g; swedes ~800 g; plum tomatoes = 400 g tins; lemon ~45 ml / lime ~30 ml juice.
Duplicate label ingredients merged (higher amount kept).
Liquid for home cooking: cook rice, quinoa, pasta, noodles and potatoes in water as you normally would (salt the water; drain where appropriate). For sauces, braises and stir-fry glazes, add water or stock gradually until the consistency is right — do not try to measure the ready-meal's residual water.
Low FODMAP: no onion or garlic bulbs — use chives / green tops only. Inspired recreation from Field Doctor ingredients, not an official recipe.
Chives listed in grams to match fresh packs (e.g. Waitrose Cooks' Ingredients Chives, 20 g).
Extra Virgin Olive Oil is kept as an ingredient on this recipe because the ready meal is relatively oil-rich (or pesto-style); still fry/roast in extra virgin olive oil as directed.
